title: Deep learning quantifies stroma-to-tumor ratio and tumor burden in luminal breast cancer
summary: In 1968 luminal breast cancer cases split into discovery (1027) and test (941) sets, deep learning quantified stroma-to-tumor ratio (S:TR), stromal spatial arrangement and tumor burden. High S:TR was linked to better survival and heterogeneous S:TR to worse outcome; tumor burden was an independent predictor (BCSS HR 1.7; DMFS HR 1.64). The analysis is retrospective and the validation is an internal split of one cohort.
ai_technology: Supervised deep learning models on whole-slide images quantifying tumor and stromal features
